spec.value: A gang that works the channel has to sleep on land. The families follow it. The camp is forty years old.
Families whose people are on the roll, living within walking distance of it.
The camp has no claim on the Hist a day upriver. The families stay because the clutch is in the shed.
A slope of firm ground above the marsh, below the Border road. The top terrace stays dry enough for a hatching shed.
If the clutch is lost, the families go somewhere the ledger cannot follow.

sockets.why: The families' store basket at the west shed.
The egg clutch inside the hatching shed.
A family cooks at the camp's fire.
Families sit on the bench by the fire after a shift.
The gang's families sleep under the west shed's thatch.
The clutch-keeper sleeps in the south tent, a few paces from the shed.
The clutch-keeper fetches dry reed for the clutch from the store basket by the shed door.
An overseer sits on the bench by the fire, with the yard and the sheds in view.
The eldest mends the nets at the corner of the west shed.
The eldest of one family sleeps under the east shed's thatch.
The hatching shed's door, where the clutch is kept.
The steep bank below the west sleeping shed, the climb down to the reeds.
The hatching shed door, the way in to the clutch.
The overseers' hut door, on the yard way.
One of the brokers' two overseers keeps the camp's count.
The clutch-keeper keeps the eggs warm and dry and rarely leaves the shed.
The families of the gang cook, mend and wait for the shift to come back.
The eldest of one family, who sees the raid from the sheds.
A sleeping place under the west shed's thatch.
The camp's fire on the middle terrace, where the families sit on the night of the raid.
The yard way between the overseers' door and the tents.
The door of the hatching shed, where the clutch-keeper comes out that night.
The yard, read back in the epilogue to show whether the families stayed.
Where the camp's way leaves the Border road, a post carries two boards along the road, one toward Stormhold and one toward Thorn.
